_comment: Guided tour for the maximum-entropy decay tool. Steps point at the real toolbar buttons and wait for the user to press them. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: What this tool answers
steps.text:
A multi-exponential fit asks which two or three lifetimes? — which presupposes there are two or three. This tool asks what distribution of decay times fits, without assuming a shape.

Five steps. You press the buttons; the tour only points at them.

steps.title: Start with a decay whose answer you know
steps.text: Load example loads a seeded bi-exponential decay (1.0 and 4.5 ns, 60:40) and reconstructs its lifetime distribution: two peaks at known places, so you can see what the method makes of them before you give it your own decay.

steps.title: Give it a decay and an IRF
steps.text:
MEM fits in convolved space like any other TCSPC analysis, so it needs the instrument response as well as the decay.

Pick both in the Input section: the curve named IRF (or prompt) is the response, else the second one picked. Refresh lists the live fits instead (then Fit takes data, range and IRF from one). An instrument response measured on a different day or at a different count rate no longer matches the data, and the mismatch will appear in the recovered distribution as structure.

await.hint: Pick a decay (and its IRF) in the Input section and press Use selected.

steps.title: Run it once, and distrust the answer
steps.text:
Press Run MEM. You get a distribution — smooth, positive, and entirely dependent on the regularization weight ν you have not chosen yet.

That is the honest state of it: the inversion is ill-posed, so ν is what decides how much structure you are shown. The next step is choosing it.

await.hint: Press Run MEM and look at the recovered distribution.

steps.title: Choose ν with the L-curve
steps.text:
Press L-curve. It sweeps ν and plots residual norm against solution norm; the corner is the standard compromise — past it, more smoothness starts costing real fit quality.

The corner is a heuristic, not a criterion with a confidence level. It is a starting point, not an answer.

await.hint: Press L-curve and note where the corner falls.

steps.title: The step that decides whether you can publish it
steps.text:
Re-run at ν a factor of two either side of the corner and compare.

Peaks that stay put are features. Peaks that move, split or vanish are regularization artefacts, and no amount of goodness-of-fit will tell you which you have — only this sweep will.

Then try a different grid range and a different prior. Structure that follows the prior is the prior showing through.

Sample gives spread on a derived quantity; Save writes the result out. Press ? for the theory.
